newsitem.title: USA: U.S. to send Perry to talks with Gulf allies.
newsitem.headline: U.S. to send Perry to talks with Gulf allies.

text.p: U.S. Defense Secretary William Perry will fly to the Gulf region to discuss the Iraqi crisis with U.S. friends and allies, defense officials said on Friday.

One administration official, who asked not to be identified, said Perry was expected to travel to Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Bahrain and Turkey. He said Perry would leave "shortly" but there was no confirmation of reports that he would go on Friday night.

His mission, undertaken as U.S. planes and ships gathered in the Gulf region to face down a challenge by Iraqi President Saddam Hussein, was intended to secure backing for possible U.S. attacks and for enforcing no-fly zones over Iraq.

The trip was discussed on Friday morning at a meeting of President Bill Clinton's top national security advisers and was expected to be discussed at another meeting later on Friday between Clinton and those same advisers, one official said.

The thinking is that Perry -- not Secretary of State Warren Christopher or some other senior official -- would go because "the focus right now is the military aspect," one administration official said.

"The purpose of the Perry trip would be to talk to regional players ... (about) providing the support we would need to carry out various operations in the region and to explain exactly what possible missions might be, in this case to keep the no-fly zone effectively in force," he added.

Although Iraq and the United States signaled a willingness on Friday to end their face-off, the Pentagon said it would watch and continue for now to build a Gulf strike force of attack jets and warships.
